subject.title: fix embedded compaction hook reset API

question: Should embedded `after_compaction` hooks gain a public current-session reset capability, and if so must it be unavailable to every other hook context?
rationale: This adds a permanent plugin contract and session-lifecycle capability; source inspection can identify safe mechanics, but it cannot establish maintainer intent for the public API surface.

options.title: Approve after-compaction only
options.body: Expose a current-session-only reset request exclusively to `after_compaction` hooks and require the outer lifecycle owner to perform it after all active handles clear.

options.title: Keep resets core-owned
options.body: Do not expose an imperative hook API; instead add a typed compaction result or other core-owned signal that requests a fresh session.

recommendation.title: Approve after-compaction only
recommendation.body: Expose a current-session-only reset request exclusively to `after_compaction` hooks and require the outer lifecycle owner to perform it after all active handles clear.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision primarily changes the plugin hook context contract, and recent hook-contract history points here most directly.
